scope: Storefront handoff and Vercel proxy readiness

tasks.description: Record current architecture, superseded proof-upload/expiry decisions, reservation policy, and phased acceptance criteria.
tasks.verification: Reviewed current worktree and prior session artifacts; captured baseline storefront tests and typecheck.

tasks.description: Implement a pure WhatsApp URL builder with international phone validation and the persisted order's complete summary.
acceptance: Encode an order reference, each line and all persisted totals.
Never imply that WhatsApp sent the message or attached proof.
tasks.verification: Three unit tests cover E.164 validation, complete encoded summary, and invalid input.

tasks.description: Navigate to WhatsApp only after order persistence, preserving a fallback for popup/configuration failures.
acceptance: A failed POST closes the temporary tab and does not hand off.
A successful POST routes the tab to the configured wa.me link.
The persisted order remains accessible with a manual fallback link and proof instructions.
tasks.verification: Inspected the order-first request flow; the confirmation page retains a fallback CTA when popup/config is unavailable.

tasks.description: Verify first-batch behavior using focused storefront tests, typecheck, and lint.
acceptance: Storefront test, typecheck, and lint commands pass or pre-existing failures are identified.

tasks.description: Harden the Next.js-to-gateway boundary for Vercel and document the separate backend requirement.
acceptance: No production proxy silently falls back to localhost.
Production gateway URLs must use HTTPS and reject credentials, query strings, and fragments.
Transient gateway outages are reported as unavailable rather than misreported as expired authentication.
Vercel documentation states that NestJS services and databases still require a separately deployed backend.
